title: Export as ZIP for WordPress and Joomla carries installer.php, and an install code travels only as a hash for a remote database
steps: S1: Run the installer unit test (serialized replace, dump reader, tar names, config editors, database host classification, install code and the attempt lock).
S2: Build a WordPress package with an install code and read its members.
S3: Build a package with no code and one with a malformed code.
S4: Build a full WordPress package end to end through the export command.
expect: S2: installer.php, README.md and index.html at the root; the code appears only as a PBKDF2-SHA256 record in install-code.json inside the tracy-package-<32 hex> folder, never in plain text in any member.
S3: no install-code.json without a code; a malformed code is refused and not echoed.
S4: one zip, uploaded once, with config placeholders, the dump unchanged and sums that hold.
evidence: Before this change the WordPress/Joomla package held only a README and the customer moved the database and config by hand
fence: Package shape and installer logic at unit level; installing on a real PHP host is covered by test/e2e/export-installer/run.sh (Docker), not by this case

tests: export-package: the install code travels only as a PBKDF2 hash
export-package: no install code, no record
export: a full WordPress point becomes one zip
